title: Dozens of Masked Settlers Besiege Qusra Homes, Trap Palestinians, Set Fires as Siege Enters Fourth Week
detail: On Saturday, August 29, 2026, dozens of masked Israeli settlers, backed by Israeli forces, attacked homes around the village of Qusra south of Nablus in the occupied West Bank — the first major flare-up since an earlier siege in the same area drew international condemnation. Settlers surrounded a Palestinian home and threw stones and flaming material while at least four residents were trapped inside; one resident said Israeli troops fired tear gas into the home and detained those inside while releasing him. Coordination was underway to let an ambulance reach the area to evacuate one injured person. The attack extended a siege that began August 9 on three homes in Qusra's Ras al-Ain area — now in its fourth week — during which settlers have cut water, electricity and supplies, burned a mosque, and attacked residents attempting to install protective window shields; a local mosque was set on fire in July. The Israeli military has declared the area a closed military zone with roadblocks at the village entrances, adding three more roadblocks in the preceding days. Resident Loui Abu Ridi said of the prolonged siege, 'We're not safe here. We fear for our own safety' — calling it 'a nightmare … 21 days.' Earlier the same day, resident Loai al-Bairoty was injured in a related incident.

title: IDF Strikes Hamas Commander Hiding at Deir al-Balah Hospital; Separate Fire Kills 3 Palestinians Including Hamouda al-Attar
detail: On Saturday, August 29, 2026, the Israeli military said it struck and killed a Hamas commander in the Deir al-Balah area of central Gaza who it said had been planning terror attacks and was found hiding within the compound of Shuhada al-Aqsa Hospital. The IDF said it took steps to reduce civilian harm and cast the strike as evidence of 'Hamas's cynical use of humanitarian infrastructure,' embedding itself within medical facilities. Separately, Israeli strikes and gunfire elsewhere in central Gaza killed three more Palestinians and wounded others the same day, according to local health officials; among the dead was Hamouda al-Attar, whose funeral was held at al-Aqsa Hospital in Deir al-Balah, with mourners photographed carrying his body. The deaths came as the toll of Palestinians killed in Gaza since the October 2025 ceasefire continued to climb despite the truce.

title: Masked Settlers Attack NBC News Crew and Palestinian Woman in Jalud; Netanyahu Breaks Silence to Condemn 'Criminal Acts of Violence' in Qusra and Jalud
detail: On Saturday, August 29, 2026, masked Israeli settlers attacked an NBC News team and a Palestinian woman, Aida Ahmed Abdullah, in the West Bank village of Jalud near Nablus. Three NBC crew members — correspondent Matt Bradley, cameraman Khaldoon Eid and producer Lawahez Jabari — were interviewing Abdullah and her family, who said they had been driven from their home by settlers, when a car with Israeli plates reversed up the hill toward them; masked men leaped out and beat the group with sticks and threw rocks before fleeing. Bradley said the attackers 'jumped out, beat us, then jumped back in the car,' while Eid said 'we didn't expect that — that they would come to attack.' Abdullah and the crew were treated for injuries; the Israel Press Council called it 'a direct violation of the public's right to know.' The Jalud attack came the same day dozens of masked settlers stormed Qusra and seized a Palestinian home with its owner inside. Later that day, Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu broke his silence to condemn the violence, saying he 'strongly condemn[s] the criminal acts of violence committed in the villages of Qusra and Jalud by a handful of rioters who are violating the law, causing a grave injustice to the law-abiding Jewish community, interfering with the IDF in carrying out its missions, and harming Israel's standing in the world.' President Isaac Herzog separately condemned the 'lawbreakers' who act 'in complete opposition to the values of Israel.'
